column1: # FH1_* flag documentation for data/settings.json (section "flags"; build.rs merges it with the scanned flag table).
# Columns (TAB-separated): NAME, AREA, DEFAULT, WHAT, EFFECT. AREA is one of build.rs AREAS; DEFAULT = on | off | <number> | unset
# (behaviour when the variable is unset). WHAT = what it does (player-facing), EFFECT = what changes in looks / gameplay / performance.
# Flags missing here fall back to their code comment. Keep one line per flag, no tabs inside fields.

column4: Overrides the Options anti-aliasing: off, fxaa, smaa, smaa2x (SMAA on MSAA 2x, the default), msaa2, msaa (4x) or old (leave cameras alone).
column5: Changes edge smoothness versus GPU cost.

column4: Chooses how ABS measures slip: v (road speed, ABS never fires), wr (wheel surface speed), anything else uses the default normalised slip.
column5: Changes ABS pulse behaviour; default matches the original.

column4: Front bumper and rear wing parts add drag and downforce. Set to 0 to ignore them.
column5: Winged cars get downforce at speed; 0 removes it.

column4: Doppler pitch shift on AI and traffic engine sounds. Set to 0 to disable.
column5: Passing cars change pitch as they go by.

column4: How many nearby AI and traffic cars get engine sounds at once.
column5: More voices make traffic louder and richer but cost audio CPU.

column4: AI cars pass and follow other cars with side clearance and braking checks. Set to 0 for the older simpler rule.
column5: AI overtakes and traffic following look more natural by default.

column4: Set to any value to log driving-line details every frame.
column5: Prints debug lines about the racing line; floods the log.

column4: Distance in metres within which AI cars are drawn.
column5: Larger shows AI cars farther away at some performance cost.

column4: Set to 0 to stop matching AI opponents to the event car class.
column5: Off can put mismatched-class cars in the field.

column4: Braking deceleration in m/s2 that AI cars plan with when closing on a car ahead.
column5: Higher lets AI cars brake later and tailgate closer.

column4: AI cars use their own AI gearbox logic. Set to 0 to use the car's normal automatic.
column5: Changes how AI cars shift and accelerate.

column4: Fraction of its tyre grip the computer drivers will use in corners.
column5: Higher makes AI cars corner faster, lower makes them slower and easier to beat.

column4: Metres after the start that an AI car keeps its grid lane before moving to the racing line; 0 means straight to the line.
column5: Longer values give a more orderly race start.

column4: Sideways speed in m/s at which AI cars move from their grid lane onto the racing line.
column5: Higher makes AI cars cut over faster after the start.

column4: Set to 0 to use the event data raw AI skill without the difficulty-based cap.
column5: Off makes AI faster and tougher in early events.

column4: AI race cars keep extra clearance from other cars and the player, treat cars close alongside as blocking, and brake earlier for a car right ahead. Set to 0 for the older margins.
column5: AI cars bump into each other and the player less; set to 0 to restore the old tighter driving.

column4: Faster AI race pace: skill margins 0.97 instead of 0.94, skill draw biased to the better half, later throttle lift in understeer. Set to 0 for the old pace.
column5: AI opponents lap a few percent quicker.

column4: A hit, spun, wrong-way or stuck AI car is put back on the racing line (no sooner than 3 s after its last reset) instead of reversing out. Set to 0 for the old reverse-out.
column5: AI cars no longer back up aggressively after a crash.

column4: A traffic car that was hit stops, pauses about 3 s, and is put back on its lane instead of reversing. Set to 0 for the old behaviour.
column5: Crashed traffic no longer drives backwards.

column4: Starts an AI-only test race on a given route (format route:count) with no barriers or race rules.
column5: Testing only: spawns AI cars on a route at startup and skips the launch menu.

column4: Set to 0 to stop placing the named leaderboard rivals above you on the grid.
column5: Off uses anonymous drivers instead of ranked rivals.

column4: Number that caps the AI skill id (1 is the fastest); unset follows difficulty: Easy 80, Medium 16, Hard 4, Pro 1 (20 / 8 / 1 with FH1_AI_GAME_DIFF=0).
column5: Lower makes AI drivers faster and harder to beat.

column4: Set to 1 to give AI and traffic cars tyre smoke too (default is the player only).
column5: More smoke on screen in races, with some fps cost.

column4: AI cars use traction control. Set to 0 to drive them without it.
column5: Without it AI cars spin wheels more and launch worse.

column4: Set to 0 to stop making AI easier when the event is below your career tier.
column5: Off keeps AI as strong as the event data says on early events.

column4: Limits the car rotation speed to 6 rad/s like the original; set to 0 to remove the limit.
column5: Prevents wild spinning; off allows faster spins.

column4: Set to 0 to turn off animated world objects entirely.
column5: Removes moving props such as animated scenery; slightly lower load.

column4: Animated objects and their textures load on a background task. Set to 0 to load inside the frame.
column5: Avoids long freezes when new animated objects load.

column4: Debug face culling for animated objects: game uses the game's mode, none draws both sides; default is flipped culling.
column5: Testing only: shows faces that are normally hidden.

column4: Path prefix; when set, writes the translated animated-object shader code to files there.
column5: Testing only: dumps shader source files to disk.

column4: Animated world objects use the game's shaders. Set to 0 to use the standard material.
column5: Changes the shading of animated props.

column4: Skinned animated objects use the game's shaders. Set to 0 to draw them with the standard material.
column5: Affects how animated skinned props look.

column4: Animated objects emit their lights (glows) near the camera. Set to 0 to disable them.
column5: Lights on moving props such as rides appear or vanish.

column4: Throttles the update rate of distant animated objects. Set to 0 to animate everything every frame.
column5: Saves CPU; 0 gives full-rate animation everywhere.

column4: Moves the camera to view a named animated object (name,distance,height).
column5: Testing only: repositions the camera for inspecting an animated object.

column4: Loads the chosen world data on a background thread; set to 0 to load it on the main thread.
column5: Smoother loading screen; off may freeze the window while loading.

column4: Set to 0 to write save/log files on the main thread instead of a background writer.
column5: Off can cause small hitches when the game saves or logs.

column4: on forces sound enabled, off silences all game audio and radio; unset plays sound except in automated agent runs.
column5: Turns the entire car audio and radio on or off.

column4: Loads the player car's sound on a background task. Set to 0 to load it inside the frame.
column5: Avoids a hitch when the car changes.

column4: Gates overrun burbles on a real throttle lift. Set to 0 for the old trigger.
column5: Burbles occur only after genuine lift-offs.

column4: File path; when set, the final in-game audio mix is also recorded to it as raw 16-bit stereo.
column5: Testing only: writes a raw audio recording to disk while playing.

column4: Engine-sound character chain (distortion, exaggerated shift cuts, backfire pops, limiter). Set to 0 for the old clean engine sound.
column5: Engines sound grittier, louder and more aggressive by default; 0 gives the cleaner stock-style mix.

column4: Part of an audio output device name; the game uses the first device whose name contains it instead of following the system default.
column5: Pins sound to a chosen speaker or headset and stops it switching when the Windows default changes.

column4: Gain of the engine sound layers (1.0 is the original level).
column5: Louder or quieter engine against turbo, tyres and other effects.

column4: Strength of the added engine grit/distortion; 0 is clean, higher is rawer.
column5: Changes how raspy and aggressive engines sound.

column4: Flattens the volume envelope of the engine bass layer. Set to 0 to keep the original envelope.
column5: Steadier engine rumble without pulsing.

column4: Makes the low-frequency engine rumble layer a seamless loop. Set to 0 for the raw clip with its gap.
column5: Removes a periodic thud in the engine bass.

column4: Set to 1 to use the short rumble clip for engines up to 6 cylinders instead of the longer pitched-down 8-cylinder loop.
column5: Changes the low-end rumble character on small engines.

column4: Extra engine loudness in dB added on top of the character chain.
column5: Makes the engine louder overall; raise it if the car sounds quiet.

column4: Level of exhaust pops, burbles and backfire crackle on lift-off and shifts; 0 removes them.
column5: More or fewer pops and burbles when you lift or shift.

column4: Volume of tyre roll and skid screech sounds.
column5: Lower for quieter tyre screeching, raise for louder.

column4: Gain of turbo spool and blow-off sounds relative to the game's own levels.
column5: Lower it to hear the raw engine more, raise it for a louder turbo whistle.

column4: Set to any value to hold full throttle with a slight steer, with no player input.
column5: Testing only: the car drives itself and the launch menu is skipped.

column4: Steering amount (-1 to 1) used by the autodrive test mode.
column5: Testing only: changes how sharply the autodriven car turns.

column4: Weights AWD power split by tyre radius; set to 0 for the older split without it.
column5: Slightly changes how AWD cars divide power between axles.

column4: Only loud bangs (upshift cracks, rev-limiter bounces) fire flames; burbles do not. Set to 0 to flame on every audible pop.
column5: Fewer flames; 0 gives flames on small crackles too.

column4: Set to 1 to draw markers at every exhaust outlet of every car and log their positions.
column5: Testing only: shows red and blue debug markers on cars.

column4: Exhaust backfire flames and flashes. Set to 0 to turn them off.
column5: No flames from the exhaust on pops and bangs.

column4: How far a pop must stand out above the engine loudness before it produces a flame.
column5: Higher means fewer flames, lower means more flames from quiet pops.

column4: Set to game to use the game's own backfire particles instead of the custom flame effect.
column5: Changes the look of exhaust flames.

column4: Backfire flames are driven only by pops that are actually audible. Set to 0 for the older unsynced triggering.
column5: Flames line up with the pop sounds you hear.

column4: Set to 0 to ignore pre-baked scenery bundles and stream everything live.
column5: Baked data loads faster; 0 is slower to stream but always uses fresh data.

column4: Set to 1 (or to a folder path) to run the engine in static-world cell bake mode and write baked cells.
column5: Testing only: a build step that forces the static world on and loads scenery for baking; not for normal play.

column4: Merges props into per-cell chunks; set to 0 to draw every prop separately.
column5: Better fps with merging; with 0 draw calls and CPU cost go up.

column4: Cell size in metres used when merging props into chunks.
column5: Larger cells mean fewer draws but coarser culling; smaller the opposite.

column4: Only each prop's coarsest LOD casts sun shadows; set to 0 so every LOD level casts in its own range.
column5: Fewer shadow draws and better fps; with 0 shadows are drawn from finer LODs.

column4: Merged prop chunks cast shadows only within their LOD range; set to 0 to make all chunks cast.
column5: Fewer shadow draws and better fps; with 0 more shadow casters are drawn.

column4: Set to 0 to stop batching small non-shadow-casting scenery together.
column5: Batching lowers draw calls; turning it off may reduce fps in dense areas.

column4: Set to relative to use the old sun/ambient light scaling (noon values scaled by brightness) instead of the game's time-of-day colours.
column5: Lighting on engine-lit objects (e.g. dusk cars) looks brighter or flatter than the default.

column4: Cars without flagged ground-contact points use points from the body bounding box. Set to 0 for none.
column5: Prevents such cars sinking into or scraping the road oddly.

column4: Body collision also tests along the car path each tick; set to 0 for the old discrete test.
column5: Fewer cars tunnelling through thin walls at high speed.

column4: Keeps the window hidden at boot until the first menu or loading frame is ready; set to 0 to show it immediately.
column5: Avoids a white or blank window flash at startup.

column4: Set to 0 to keep brake lights steady instead of pulsing dark while ABS releases a wheel.
column5: Off gives constant brake lights; default flickers with ABS activity.

column4: Multiplier on brake strength; 1.0 is the game's value, higher brakes harder, lower softer.
column5: Changes stopping distances and how easily the wheels lock or ABS kicks in.

column4: Applies brake torque inside the wheel solver with the game smooth sign; set to 0 for the old lock clamp after the solve.
column5: More accurate braking and ABS behaviour, especially at low speed.

column4: Uses the full camera effect layers from the car data. Set to 0 to use the set without effects.
column5: Changes how much the cameras sway and react.

column4: Number of the camera view to start in (0-4).
column5: Testing only: starts the game in a chosen camera view.

column4: File path; when set, the chase camera writes a log of its state to it.
column5: Testing only: writes camera log data to disk.

column4: Set to 0 to keep the simple glTF car body instead of the game's own car body shaders (faithful renderer only; the Remaster renderer ignores this).
column5: 0 makes cars look flatter and less like the original; no effect in the Remaster renderer.

column4: Set to 1 to run an automatic A/B comparison toggling the game car shaders during the run.
column5: Testing only: car body look flips back and forth while comparing; faithful renderer only.

column4: Set to 0 to decode car paint and shader colours with the old raw/PWL conversion instead of the game's sRGB conversion.
column5: 0 shifts car colours (for example the teal glass and the paint hue) away from the original.

column4: Overrides a car material constant as tech:Name=x,y,z,w; entries separated by semicolons, * for all techniques.
column5: Testing only: arbitrary car shader tweaking for debugging.

column4: Overrides face culling per car shader technique as tech:none|flip, comma separated, * for all.
column5: Testing only: can make car parts disappear or turn inside out.

column4: Set to 0 to always set the car dynamic-light registers, even when no headlight is on.
column5: No visible change; 0 restores an old register difference from the game (faithful car shaders).

column4: Path of a file to append JSON dumps of every car shader constant and global to.
column5: Testing only: writes debug data to disk when cars load.

column4: Seconds after start at which the car shader globals are dumped to the FH1_CARFX_DUMP file.
column5: Testing only: timing of a debug dump.

column4: Set to 0 to skip the extra reflection layer on car headlight/taillight glass lenses.
column5: 0 removes the glossy reflection on lamp lenses (faithful car shaders).

column4: Set to 0 to stop lamp covers writing depth; ab flips it periodically for testing.
column5: 0 can bring back lamp covers popping in and out or being painted over by bulb layers.

column4: Set to 1 to enable a special draw order for lamp lenses; ab flips it periodically for comparison.
column5: Experimental lamp ordering with no measured effect; ab is a test mode that flips it every 20 frames.

column4: Any value prints one log line per car part with its material, technique and textures, plus car shader globals.
column5: Testing only: spams the log when a car loads.

column4: Set to 0 to stop sorting car parts in file order when drawing transparent parts; ab flips it periodically for testing.
column5: 0 can bring back flicker/popping of lamp covers; ab is a test mode.

column4: Set to 1 to tint every car shader technique with the car's paint colour, as the older code did.
column5: 1 can wrongly paint non-body parts (such as trim) in the car colour; default paints body techniques only.

column4: Comma list of car shader technique names to leave out entirely.
column5: Testing only: hides the car parts using those techniques.

column4: Seconds after start at which the game simulates a single press of the next-car key.
column5: Testing only: automatically switches car once for automated runs.

column4: Folder to write each car shader technique's translated WGSL source into.
column5: Testing only: writes shader files to disk; no visual change.

column4: Set to 0 to use the basic glTF wheels instead of the game-shaded wheels (also off with FH1_CARFX=0).
column5: Wheels lose the game's rim shading and detail.

column4: Set to 0 to use the lower-detail wheel model instead of the high-detail LOD0 rim.
column5: Rims look less detailed with 0.

column4: Set to 0 to load cars in the main update instead of on a background thread.
column5: Off causes longer stalls when swapping or spawning a car.

column4: Set to 0 to stop the car from casting into the main shadow cascades.
column5: 0 removes the car's real-time shadow (the drop shadow still shows) and saves GPU time.

column4: Face culling for the car shadow casters: 0 two-sided, 1 cull back faces, 2 cull front faces.
column5: Changes shadow acne on the car body; the default is chosen to avoid it.

column4: Set to 0 to give every car part its own shadow-caster proxy instead of one merged proxy per node.
column5: 0 costs many more draws for car shadows (lower fps); same shadow shape.

column4: Distance in metres car shadow-caster surfaces are pushed inward to cut self-shadowing; 0 disables.
column5: Higher values reduce shadow streaks on the car body but can thin the shadow.

column4: Seconds the N/P car-switch keys must rest before the new car is actually loaded (0 loads every car scrolled past).
column5: Higher avoids hitches while cycling cars quickly; 0 loads each car instantly.

column4: Set to 0 to stop cars getting dirty from driving.
column5: The car stays clean instead of gathering dirt over distance.

column4: Set to 0 to stop correcting car lighting constants to match the game's own values.
column5: 0 gives the old, slightly different car lighting (faithful car shaders only).

column4: Set to 0 to read car files on the main thread instead of waiting for a background prefetch.
column5: 0 can cause freezes of several seconds when cars load; default makes parts appear a few frames later.

column4: Multiplier for the strength of environment reflections on game-shaded car bodies; 0 = no reflection.
column5: Higher gives shinier, more mirror-like paint; 0 gives matte paint (faithful car shaders only).

column4: Extra shadow receiver bias in metres on cars; hides self-shadow crawling on lamps and bumpers.
column5: Lower brings back flickering streaks on the car; higher softens its self-shadowing.

column4: Two comma-separated multipliers (ambient and directional) on the car's hemispherical ambient lighting.
column5: Higher values brighten the ambient light on car bodies; faithful car shaders only.

column4: Applies contrast-adaptive sharpening after upscaling; set to 0 to turn it off.
column5: Sharper image when render scale is below 100%; off gives a softer picture.

column4: Sharpening amount from 0.0 to 1.0 for contrast-adaptive sharpening.
column5: Higher values give a crisper but possibly over-sharpened image.

column4: Builds the car catalog (details panel stats) on a background thread at startup; set to 0 to build it when the menu opens.
column5: Avoids a hitch on first opening the car browser; 0 brings the hitch back.

column4: Set to 0 to stop tracking the player car class and upgrade build for race field matching.
column5: Off makes AI fields ignore your car upgrades.

column4: Seconds added to the cloud animation clock at start so screenshots match a reference.
column5: Testing only: clouds start at a different position.

column4: Set to 1 to re-enable GPU light clustering.
column5: Off by default (saves about 1 ms per frame); on may look identical but costs fps.

column4: Shows a +N CR notification when you gain credits; set to 0 to hide them.
column5: Fewer on-screen popups when off.

column4: 0 turns crowds off, all draws every crowd object including event crowds, walkers selects walkers; unset draws the named festival crowds.
column5: Controls how many spectators and walkers are in the world.

column4: Set to 1 to run an in-process A/B timing comparison of crowd rendering modes.
column5: Testing only: changes crowd rendering while it measures.

column4: Brightness multiplier for crowd cards.
column5: Makes spectators brighter or darker.

column4: Crowd cards are lit by the sun and ambient light. Set to 0 for unlit cards.
column5: Crowds match the time of day; 0 looks flat and bright.

column4: Crowd cards are merged per cell. Set to 0 to draw one card object per spectator.
column5: Merged cells reduce draw overhead; 0 uses more entities.

column4: Set to 1 to use the old model orientation, in which crowd figures showed their backs and walkers walked backwards.
column5: Restores the earlier wrong facing; only for comparison.

column4: 3D crowd figures are animated on the GPU. Set to 0 for the CPU path.
column5: Faster crowds with less CPU use.

column4: Crowd walkers are moved on the GPU. Set to 0 to walk them on the CPU.
column5: Lower CPU cost for walkers; 0 is the old slower path.

column4: Sign (1 or -1) applied to crowd card heading; a debug fix for facing.
column5: Testing only: flips which way crowd cards face.

column4: Set to 1 to draw crowd cards per object instead of merged per cell.
column5: Used for performance comparison; more entities.

column4: Degrees of yaw applied to 3D crowd figures so they face the right way.
column5: Rotates all spectator figures.

column4: Distance in metres within which crowd members are 3D figures instead of flat cards; default comes from the track settings.
column5: Larger shows more 3D spectators at more cost.

column4: Pre-reads crowd model files in the background. Set to 0 to skip.
column5: Fewer hitches when crowds first appear; slightly more memory use.

column4: Maximum 3D crowd figures created per frame; 0 means unlimited.
column5: Lower avoids hitches when crowds load; higher fills them in sooner.

column4: Pause menu shows the Garage page (Change car / Customize); set to 0 to go straight to the car list.
column5: Enables or hides the paint, rims and kit customisation menus.

column4: The Garage, My cars, Autoshow and Customize pages are controller-friendly card menus (cards with photos, class badges, prices, stat bars and live previews); set to 0 for the old list pages.
column5: Looks and navigation only; 0 restores the previous list menus with the same shop and customize rules.

column4: Set to 0 to start with the diagnostics overlay hidden (F3 toggles it).
column5: Shows or hides the FPS and resource overlay at startup.

column4: Path to the extracted game disc folder, used as a fallback source for traffic settings and by data-parsing tests (defaults to the repo disc folder).
column5: Testing only: only matters when converted game data is missing; no change in normal play.

column4: Reflects engine inertia onto the driven wheels while the clutch is engaged; set to 0 for the old behaviour that ignored it.
column5: Slightly changes acceleration feel and how quickly wheels spin up.

column4: Set to 1 to use the older chevron racing line that slides with the car instead of the game's world-anchored strip.
column5: Changes the look of the driving line on the road.

column4: Set to 0 to turn off the soft contact shadow drawn under cars.
column5: 0 removes the dark patch under the car, making cars look less grounded.

column4: Any value switches the drop shadow to a debug display mode.
column5: Testing only: draws the car drop shadow in a debug visualization.

column4: Distance in metres beyond which other cars' contact shadows are hidden and not updated; 0 = always update.
column5: Higher shows distant car shadows but costs CPU; lower saves performance on traffic and AI cars.

column4: Set to 0 to rewrite the car drop-shadow mesh and material every frame instead of only when something changed.
column5: 0 costs a little CPU each frame; no visual change.

column4: Any value logs car drop-shadow setup details (parts found, triangle counts, peak darkness).
column5: Testing only: log output; no visual change.

column4: Set to 1 to put GPU crowd figures and swapped glTF (FxRawStandard) materials back into Bevy's depth prepass.
column5: The prepass only feeds contact shadows; off saves GPU time, but those objects then cast no contact shadows.

column4: Set to 0 to remove the invisible walls along unfenced paved road edges.
column5: Without them you can drive off road edges and fall out of the map.

column4: The newer engine model with drag at the rev limiter and proper engine braking; set to 0 for the old model.
column5: Changes engine braking when lifting off and behaviour at the limiter.

column4: Engine torque rolls the car body like the original; set to 0 to disable.
column5: Body leans when revving or launching; off removes that lean.

column4: Set to 0 to turn off the live reflection cube that updates car reflections as you drive.
column5: Car reflections become static; a bit faster.

column4: Set to 1 to switch the live reflection cube on and off every 5 seconds and log mean frame time of each.
column5: Testing only: reflections flip on and off while running.

column4: Render a reflection cube face only every N-th frame.
column5: Higher saves GPU time but reflections update more slowly.

column4: Number of cube faces rendered per update (1 to 6).
column5: More faces keep reflections fresher but cost GPU time.

column4: Set to off to switch the reflection camera off on frames with no face (experimental); default keeps it active.
column5: Rarely helps; can cause hitches or worse frame times.

column4: Maximum number of meshes drawn into the reflection cube (default from the track settings).
column5: Higher shows more in reflections but costs more GPU/CPU.

column4: Any value logs which big meshes and how many candidates go into the reflection cube.
column5: No visible change; adds log lines.

column4: Maximum bounding radius in metres for scenery drawn into the reflection cube.
column5: Lowering it hides huge backdrop meshes from reflections.

column4: Minimum bounding radius in metres for scenery to be drawn into the reflection cube.
column5: Raising it drops small objects from reflections for speed.

column4: Set to 0 to use six separate face cameras instead of one persistent camera re-aimed each update.
column5: Same image; 0 can cause extra CPU work and hitches.

column4: File path (.ppm) to save the six reflection cube faces to after a few seconds.
column5: Testing only: writes an image file.

column4: Seconds after start at which the reflection cube screenshot is taken.
column5: Testing only: only matters with FH1_ENVCUBE_SHOT.

column4: Edge size in pixels of the live reflection cube map (16 to 2048).
column5: Larger is sharper car reflections but costs GPU time and memory.

column4: Minimum apparent size (radius over distance) a mesh needs to appear in the reflection cube; default comes from the track settings.
column5: Lower includes more distant objects in reflections at higher cost.

column4: One flame per exhaust pipe. Set to 0 to merge pipes closer than 11 cm into one flame.
column5: Twin-pipe cars get a flame from each pipe.

column4: Set to 1 to draw the distant backdrop in the old tile-streaming mode.
column5: Shows far scenery but may add stray pieces near the play area; only relevant when zones are off.

column4: Set to 0 to shut down normally instead of ending the process quickly once logs are saved.
column5: Off can make quitting take several seconds with a big world loaded.

column4: Path to the ffmpeg program used to decode console audio; otherwise ffmpeg on PATH is used.
column5: Only matters when converting game audio during setup.

column4: Set to 0 to turn off the in-memory cache of game files read by the renderer.
column5: 0 means more disk reads and likely hitches when loading cars and effects.

column4: Size in megabytes of the RAM cache that holds car files (textures, shader settings, models) so spawning a car does not read the disk mid-frame.
column5: Larger keeps more cars in RAM and avoids spawn hitches; smaller saves memory.

column4: Brightness multiplier of the backfire flame sprites.
column5: Higher gives brighter, bolder flames.

column4: Flames light up the bumper and road with a brief flash. Set to 0 to disable the flash.
column5: Backfire bangs briefly illuminate the surroundings.

column4: Peak brightness (lumens) of the backfire flash light.
column5: Higher makes bang flashes brighter on the road and car.

column4: Set to old to use the earlier cone-shaped flame meshes instead of the flame shader.
column5: Changes the look of exhaust flames.

column4: Name of a fog template from the track's fog list to force everywhere instead of letting zones pick their own.
column5: Testing only: fog look stays fixed across the whole map.

column4: Frames-per-second limit (a number above 1); setting it also turns the frame pacer on.
column5: Caps fps to lower heat/power use or even out pacing.

column4: Set to 1 (or ab) to enable the CPU frame pacer that waits to even out frame delivery.
column5: Measured to worsen frame jitter, so it is off; may change smoothness.

column4: Any value logs mean and max frame time every 2 seconds.
column5: No visible change; adds log lines.

column4: Applies the game's friction-torque modification to tyre yaw torque in Normal steering; set to 0 for unmodified torque.
column5: Changes how much the car rotates or resists rotating when steering hard.

column4: Shader debug: <effect hash hex>:<mode> replaces that effect's output with a debug colour; append +nocull for two-sided draw.
column5: Testing only: one surface type shows debug colours.

column4: Set to 0 to remove the small depth offset given to road decals and other blended track surfaces.
column5: Without it some decals flicker or fight with the road where they face the camera.

column4: Path of a shader file that a unit test translates and prints (cargo test only).
column5: Testing only: no effect in the game.

column4: How different in distance (relative) the half-resolution samples may be from a pixel before the blend switches from smooth to nearest-depth at edges.
column5: Higher = smoother but haloes around car and scenery edges; lower = crisper edges but blockier smoke.
